Senses.Explanation: To burn incense is a literal action whose purpose changes with the surrounding ceremony. The Collection for Resolving Chan Doubts narrates incense burned before a sacred image while establishing an oath. Huayan Shengke directly tells an unnamed monastic interlocutor to go light incense; Daxiu Zhu’s biography records incense burned before a prayer to celestial protectors and the buddhas; and the record of Fushi Qiyuan describes distant and nearby mourners burning incense and weeping at his death. Oath, instruction, prayer, and mourning are distinct settings for the same incense-burning action; none of these witnesses says that incense is burned into the body.
